reasons.specificity: The analysis closely tracks the 2001 entrepreneurial-dynamic use and the 2022 epistemic, universalism, and self-description use, with source-specific tables.
reasons.anchoring: Nearly all quoted anchors occur and support their findings, including the subsistence limit, Abrahamic scope, myth-cycle distinction, and ultimate-questions limit.
reasons.non_obviousness: It usefully distinguishes common intermediaries from direct transmission, functional substitution from identity, and market universalism from religious community.
reasons.coherence: The main synthesis is consistent, but the claimed Weber divergence conflicts with the analysis’s own later qualification and the 2001 text’s explicit use of the same signal-to-substance transformation.
reasons.usefulness: The two requested tables clearly inventory changed purposes, retained conditions, acknowledgments, and transmission status, though extensive audit metadata and duplicated scope material impede desk use.
reasons.hallucination_risk: Substantive claims are mostly bounded, but unsupported workflow assertions such as verified anchors, lost evidence, malformed scope records, and review states are presented as facts not established by the supplied sources.

decisive_errors.claim: The analysis says the 2022 Weberian finding is “restored” and frames the works as diverging because 2001 declines Weber while 2022 retains the signal-to-substance transformation.
decisive_errors.counter_passage: The 2001 source itself says, “what the ethics of ascetic protestantism had interpreted only as a signal of salvation became the message itself in the capitalist system,” so it already retains substantially the same specific Weberian transformation while declining only the broader causal-background route.

score.one_line: A highly source-specific and well-anchored inventory whose strongest weakness is an overstated Weber divergence plus unsupported audit-process metadata.
